title: Distinct Surface and Bulk Superconductivity in the Kagome Superconductor SrSn$_3$
authors: Qun Zhu, Yong-Wei Wang, Ji-Hai Zhang, Qiang-Jun Cheng, Chen-Yu Hu, Jun-Zhong Wang, Qi-Kun Xue, Xu-Cun Ma, Can-Li Song
abstract: Surface and bulk superconductivity may possess fundamentally different superconducting properties in quantum materials with nontrivial electronic structures, yet their superimposed spectroscopic signatures often prevent direct experimental access to each superconducting channel. Here we reveal, in epitaxial films of the kagome superconductor SrSn$_3$, distinct surface and bulk superconducting channels with markedly different superconducting gaps, upper critical fields, and vortex-core electronic states by tuning the tunneling junction resistance in scanning tunneling spectroscopy. The surface superconductivity is characterized by a thickness-independent superconducting gap and an enhanced upper critical field, whereas the bulk superconducting channel exhibits a larger superconducting gap that decreases with reducing film thickness and a much lower upper critical field. Within magnetic vortex cores, robust non-split zero-bias conductance peaks are observed exclusively in the surface superconducting channel, while pronounced zero-bias suppression is consistently associated with the bulk superconducting channel. These findings demonstrate that the vortex-core electronic structure depends sensitively on the underlying superconducting channel, providing new insight into vortex-bound states in topological quantum materials.
summary: This work reveals that the Kagome superconductor $	ext{SrSn}_3$ exhibits distinct surface and bulk superconducting states. By tuning the tunneling junction resistance in STS, the researchers spectroscopically separated these two channels, finding they possess different gaps and critical fields. This provides new insight into how the superconducting environment dictates vortex-bound electronic states in topological materials.
main_problem: The study aims to spectroscopically distinguish between potentially distinct superconducting surface and bulk channels in quantum materials, as their signals often overlap experimentally.
main_result: The researchers successfully demonstrated the coexistence of two distinct superconducting channels ($\Delta_s$ and $\Delta_b$) in $	ext{SrSn}_3$, characterized by different gaps, upper critical fields, and unique vortex-core electronic signatures.
method: They employed high-resolution Scanning Tunneling Spectroscopy (STS) on epitaxial films, systematically tuning the tunneling junction resistance ($R_N$) to selectively probe the surface or bulk superconducting states.
model_or_system: The physical system is epitaxial thin films of the Kagome superconductor $	ext{SrSn}_3$. The analysis relies on interpreting the differential conductance ($	ext{d}I/	ext{d}V$) spectra as a function of applied magnetic field and tunneling junction resistance.
key_observables: Superconducting gaps ($\Delta_s$ and $\Delta_b$), upper critical fields ($B_{c2}$), and zero-bias conductance peaks (ZBCPs) within magnetic vortex cores.
important_parameters: Tunneling junction resistance ($R_N$), film thickness, and applied magnetic field ($B$).
main_assumptions: The separation of the two superconducting channels is achieved by tuning $R_N$, and the observed spectral evolution directly maps to the underlying physical channels.
figures_summary: Figures show the systematic evolution of the superconducting gap with $R_N$, the thickness dependence of both gaps, and distinct vortex-core spectra (ZBCP vs. zero-bias suppression) depending on the probed channel.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for channel-selective spectroscopy, presents evidence for two distinct gaps ($\Delta_s$ and $\Delta_b$) tunable by $R_N$, and uses vortex-core states to confirm the distinct nature of the surface and bulk superconducting channels.
why_interesting: The ability to use a tunable spectroscopic probe ($R_N$) to decouple multiple superconducting orders is a powerful technique for understanding complex, multi-band superconductivity, which has implications for topological superconductivity.
